1 --- 2 title: Unsupported database features (Prisma Migrate) 3 description: How to include unsupported database features for projects that use Prisma Migrate. 4 url: /orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/unsupported-database-features 5 metaTitle: 'Prisma Migrate: Unsupported database features' 6 metaDescription: How to include unsupported database features for projects that use Prisma Migrate. 7 --- 8 9 Prisma Migrate uses the Prisma schema to determine what features to create in the database. However, some database features [cannot be represented in the Prisma schema](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/unsupported-database-features) , including but not limited to: 10 11 - Stored procedures 12 - Triggers 13 - Views 14 - Partial indexes 15 16 To add an unsupported feature to your database, you must [customize a migration](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/customizing-migrations) to include that feature before you apply it. 17 18 :::tip 19 20 The Prisma schema is able to represent [unsupported field types](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/unsupported-database-features#unsupported-field-types) and [native database functions](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/native-database-functions). 21 22 ::: 23 24 :::warning 25 26 This guide **does not apply for MongoDB**.
27 Instead of `migrate dev`, [`db push`](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/prototyping-your-schema) is used for [MongoDB](/orm/v6/overview/databases/mongodb). 28 29 ::: 30 31 ## Customize a migration to include an unsupported feature 32 33 To customize a migration to include an unsupported feature: 34 35 1. Use the `--create-only` flag to generate a new migration without applying it: 36 37 ```npm 38 npx prisma migrate dev --create-only 39 ``` 40 41 1. Open the generated `migration.sql` file and add the unsupported feature - for example, a partial index: 42 43 ```sql 44 CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tests_success_constraint 45 ON posts (subject, target) 46 WHERE success; 47 ``` 48 49 1. Apply the migration: 50 51 ```npm 52 npx prisma migrate dev 53 ``` 54 55 1. Commit the modified migration to source control. 56

However, some database features [cannot be represented in the Prisma schema](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/unsupported-database-features) , including but not limited to: - Stored procedures - Triggers - Views - Partial indexes To add an unsupported feature to your database, you must [customize a migration](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/customizing-migrations) to include that feature before you apply it. :::tip The Prisma schema is able to represent [unsupported field types](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/unsupported-database-features#unsupported-field-types) and [native database functions](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/native-database-functions). ::: :::warning This guide **does not apply for MongoDB**.
Instead of `migrate dev`, [`db push`](/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/prototyping-your-schema) is used for [MongoDB](/orm/v6/overview/databases/mongodb). ::: ## Customize a migration to include an unsupported feature To customize a migration to include an unsupported feature: 1. Use the `--create-only` flag to generate a new migration without applying it: ```npm npx prisma migrate dev --create-only ``` 1. Open the generated `migration.sql` file and add the unsupported feature - for example, a partial index: ```sql CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tests_success_constraint ON posts (subject, target) WHERE success; ``` 1. Apply the migration: ```npm npx prisma migrate dev ``` 1. Commit the modified migration to source control.

1	---
2	title: Check constraints
3	description: Learn how to configure CHECK constraints for data validation with Prisma ORM and PostgreSQL
4	url: /orm/v7/more/troubleshooting/check-constraints
5	metaTitle: Data validation with CHECK constraints (PostgreSQL)
6	metaDescription: Learn how to configure CHECK constraints for data validation with Prisma ORM and PostgreSQL by following the step-by-step instructions in this practical guide.
7	---
8	
9	This page explains how to configure [check constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.4/ddl-constraints.html#DDL-CONSTRAINTS-CHECK-CONSTRAINTS) in a PostgreSQL database. A check constraint is a condition that must be satisfied before a value can be saved to a table - for example, the discounted price of a product must always be less than the original price.
10	
11	Check constraints can be added when you create the table (using `CREATE TABLE`) or to a table that already exists (using `ALTER TABLE`).
12	
13	## Prerequisites
14	
15	- A [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) database server running
16	- The [`psql`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/13/app-psql.html) command line client
17	- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) installed
18	
19	## Single column check constraint
20	
21	Create a table with a check constraint on a single column:
22	
23	```sql
24	CREATE TABLE "public"."product" (
25	  price NUMERIC CONSTRAINT price_value_check CHECK (price > 0.01 AND price <> 1240.00)
26	);
27	ALTER TABLE "public"."product"
28	  ADD COLUMN "productid" serial,
29	  ADD PRIMARY KEY ("productid");
30	```
31	
32	This ensures the price is never less than 0.01 and never equal to 1240.00.
33	
34	## Multi-column check constraint
35	
36	Create a table with a check constraint that compares values of two columns:
37	
38	```sql
39	CREATE TABLE "public"."anotherproduct" (
40	  reducedprice NUMERIC CONSTRAINT reduced_price_check CHECK (price > reducedprice),
41	  price NUMERIC
42	);
43	ALTER TABLE "public"."anotherproduct"
44	  ADD COLUMN "productid" serial,
45	  ADD PRIMARY KEY ("productid");
46	```
47	
48	This ensures `reducedprice` is always less than `price`.
49	
50	## Multiple check constraints
51	
52	```sql
53	CREATE TABLE "public"."secondtolastproduct" (
54	  reducedprice NUMERIC CONSTRAINT reduced_price_check CHECK (price > reducedprice),
55	  price NUMERIC,
56	  tags TEXT[] CONSTRAINT tags_contains_product CHECK ('product' = ANY(tags))
57	);
58	ALTER TABLE "public"."secondtolastproduct"
59	  ADD COLUMN "productid" serial,
60	  ADD PRIMARY KEY ("productid");
61	```
62	
63	## Adding check constraints to existing tables
64	
65	```sql
66	CREATE TABLE "public"."lastproduct" (
67	  category TEXT
68	);
69	
70	ALTER TABLE "public"."lastproduct"
71	  ADD CONSTRAINT "category_not_clothing" CHECK (category <> 'clothing');
72	```
73	
74	## Using with Prisma ORM
75	
76	After introspection, your Prisma schema will include the models but the check constraints are enforced at the database level:
77	
78	```prisma
79	model product {
80	  price     Float?
81	  productid Int    @id
82	}
83	
84	model anotherproduct {
85	  price        Float?
86	  productid    Int    @id
87	  reducedprice Float?
88	}
89	```
90	
91	Generate Prisma Client and test:
92	
93	```js
94	const { PrismaClient } = require("../prisma/generated/client");
95	
96	const prisma = new PrismaClient();
97	
98	async function main() {
99	  // This will fail due to the check constraint
100	  const newProduct = await prisma.product.create({
101	    data: {
102	      price: 0.0, // violates price > 0.01
103	    },
104	  });
105	}
106	
107	main();
108	```
109	
110	The script throws an error indicating the `price_check_value` check constraint was not met:
111	
112	```
113	Error: new row for relation "product" violates check constraint "price_value_check"
114	```
115	
116	Check constraints are resolved in alphabetical order, and only the first constraint to fail appears in the error message.
117

content.text:
Neither option is ideal as phrased. The docs say to use `--create-only` and edit the migration before applying it.

- Run `npx prisma migrate dev --create-only`. This generates the migration without applying it.
- Open the generated `migration.sql` and add your constraint, e.g. `ALTER TABLE "x" ADD CONSTRAINT "name" CHECK (...);`.
- Run `npx prisma migrate dev` to apply it, then commit the migration.
- This is closest to your option 1, but edit the migration before it is applied. If it has already been applied, editing it causes drift or checksum issues. In that case, use a new migration (your option 2) with `--create-only`. Prisma docs don't state this second case, so it's my inference.
- Check constraints aren't representable in the Prisma schema. They are enforced only at the database level.

Sources: `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v6/prisma-migrate/workflows/unsupported-database-features.mdx` ("Customize a migration to include an unsupported feature"); `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/more/troubleshooting/check-constraints.mdx` ("Adding check constraints to existing tables", "Using with Prisma ORM").
